author: Ziyaad Manie, CFA
title: Introduction Alphabet/Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL
text:
Introduction 
Alphabet/Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) is a behemoth. With $111bn in revenue generated in FY17, exceptionally high profit margins and net cash on balance sheet of almost $100bn, it is amongst the three most financially robust companies in the entire world, alongside Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ). The company is blessed with an enormous competitive advantage through its ownership of the dominant search engine and video-streaming service (Google & YouTube, respectively). The management team is world class, and the company is often ranked as one of the top 3 employers in the world ( 100 Best Companies to Work For 2017 ). It is undeniably a wonderful company, and, as Warren Buffett famously said, it is “far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price” . Following a c. 13% reduction in the share price in recent weeks from its 52 week high (brought about due to a Q4 earnings “miss” and a broader market sell-off), I believe Alphabet is trading at a compelling discount to the fair value of its core operating business. The discount is made more attractive by the fact that there is considerable upside potential from its various moonshot projects via the Other Bets division. The market is likely making a big mistake by penalizing Alphabet for the Other Bets losses instead of assigning value to the option inherent in the Other Bets division.
